info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package company is incorporation end to end: pick a structure, add founders, pay, file, and e-sign.

get.summary: Get returns the caller org's formation and the stages reachable from it, or 404 when the org has not begun one.
get.description:
Get returns the caller org's formation and the stages reachable from it, or 404
when the org has not begun one.

post.summary: Begin starts the org's one formation and returns it with the stages reachable from it.
post.description:
Begin starts the org's one formation and returns it with the stages reachable
from it. It is idempotent: an org that already has a formation gets that one
back with 200, while a first call creates it and answers 201.

post.summary: Advance runs the ONE guarded transition of the formation machine.
post.description:
Advance runs the ONE guarded transition of the formation machine. It is the
only door between stages: the actions populate data, this decides ordering.

An edge the machine does not define answers 409; an edge whose guard is not yet
satisfied answers 422 naming what is missing. Reaching the terminal `company`
stage also records the incorporation on the canonical cap table, and that must
succeed before the transition is persisted.

post.summary: Renders the formation documents for the chosen structure and jurisdiction, ingests each into the org's data room, and submits the state filing through the filing seam.
post.description:
Renders the formation documents for the chosen structure and
jurisdiction, ingests each into the org's data room, and submits the state
filing through the filing seam.

With no filing partner wired the filing is recorded honestly as "manual" — no
filing id is fabricated. Available only at the documents stage.

post.summary: Sends the generated formation documents for signature by every founder and records the provider's reference on the formation.
post.description:
Sends the generated formation documents for signature by every
founder and records the provider's reference on the formation. Available only
at the esign stage.

post.summary: Records whether the formation documents have been signed.
post.description:
Records whether the formation documents have been signed. It
consults the e-signature provider, which a real provider's webhook drives; the
signal is idempotent.

An explicit `signed` in the request overrides the provider's answer, which is
the manual path for the stub provider that never self-completes.

Replaces the formation's founders. Each founder needs a name, an
email and an equity share in basis points; every founder is (re)set to pending
KYC, so a previously settled decision does not survive a change of the list.

post.summary: Share a pitch deck in the org's data room
post.description:
Stores the request body as a document in the caller org's data room and answers with the data room id to reference it by. The deck is RAW BYTES of whatever content type is sent — a PDF, a slide export — not a JSON document: the Content-Type header is carried through to the data room as given, and `?name=` names the document, defaulting to `pitch-deck`.

Scoped to the caller's validated org, and only after incorporation: a formation still short of stage `company` is refused 409 and an org that never began one is 404. The route is registered AHEAD of the surface's JSON body cap deliberately, so a deck's size ceiling is the edge's rather than the cap meant for small structured records. An empty body is 400; a data room that will not take the bytes is 502.

post.summary: Records a fundraising round on the org's canonical cap table.
post.description:
Records a fundraising round on the org's canonical cap table.
Available only after incorporation (stage company); roundType defaults to
PRICED.

post.summary: Raises an e-signature request over documents already in the org's data room — a SAFE, a convertible note, or any other fundraising paper.
post.description:
Raises an e-signature request over documents already in the org's
data room — a SAFE, a convertible note, or any other fundraising paper.
Available only after incorporation (stage company).

post.summary: Seeds the canonical cap table with the founding allocation (stakeholders, a common share class, issued shares) and anchors the deterministic equity-genesis root on-chain.
post.description:
Seeds the canonical cap table with the founding allocation
(stakeholders, a common share class, issued shares) and anchors the
deterministic equity-genesis root on-chain.

It is idempotent: once a root is recorded the cap table is NOT re-seeded, which
would double-issue founder share certificates. The root is persisted even when
the on-chain submit fails, because the root is the tamper-evident witness and
must not be recomputed on retry. Available only at the genesis stage.

post.summary: Reads an existing company's cap table from a Google Sheet and adds its stakeholders to the canonical cap table.
post.description:
Reads an existing company's cap table from a Google Sheet and
adds its stakeholders to the canonical cap table.

The first row is a header and columns are matched by name (case-insensitive):
name and email are required, type/relationship/institution optional. A sheet
without name and email columns, or with no usable data rows, is refused with
400. Available only at the import stage.

post.summary: Ingests an existing company's corporate documents from a Google Drive folder into the org's data room.
post.description:
Ingests an existing company's corporate documents from a Google
Drive folder into the org's data room. The import is shallow — sub-folders are
skipped, not walked — and available only at the import stage.

post.summary: StartKYC opens an identity-verification session for every founder with the wired provider and records each session's reference on the formation.
post.description:
StartKYC opens an identity-verification session for every founder with the
wired provider and records each session's reference on the formation.

A start is never a decision: any terminal status the provider reports at
inquiry time is clamped back to pending, so the payment gate can never open
here. A terminal status arrives only from POST /v1/company/kyc/refresh (the
provider) or POST /v1/company/kyc/decision (a Hanzo platform reviewer).

post.summary: DecideKYC records a privileged reviewer's MANUAL decision on a founder's KYC — the human-in-the-loop path, and the ONLY route to a pass when no real provider is wired.
post.description:
DecideKYC records a privileged reviewer's MANUAL decision on a founder's KYC —
the human-in-the-loop path, and the ONLY route to a pass when no real provider
is wired. It produces a DISTINCT reviewer_confirmed, never a provider
"verified".

Because Hanzo forms the entity and carries the formation KYC/AML obligation,
the reviewer is a HANZO platform reviewer (SuperAdmin), and the decision is
ATTRIBUTED to them.

post.summary: RefreshKYC reconciles each pending founder's KYC with the WIRED provider — the PULL path to a provider-reported terminal status.
post.description:
RefreshKYC reconciles each pending founder's KYC with the WIRED provider — the
PULL path to a provider-reported terminal status. For the manual provider the
check stays pending; for a real provider it reflects the settled decision,
ATTRIBUTED to the provider.

It NEVER trusts a client-asserted status — the status comes from the provider
seam — so a client cannot force a pass here, and an already-passing founder
(e.g. a reviewer confirmation) is left untouched.

post.summary: Charge the one-time formation fee and mark the formation paid
post.description:
Bills the caller's own org the one-time Hanzo Company formation fee — $999 unless the deployment sets another — and answers with the formation record carrying its paid flag and the charge reference. Takes no body: the org is the validated tenant and the amount is the platform's, never the caller's to assert.

IDEMPOTENT on the formation rather than on the request: an already-paid formation answers 200 with the same record and is not charged again, so a retry or a double-clicked button costs nothing. Available only at the `payment` stage (409 anywhere else) and only for an org that has begun a formation (404 otherwise).

A refused charge answers the fleet-wide billing contract, not a formation error — 402 when the org cannot pay, 503 when metering is unavailable — which is exactly why this route is not a typed op.

get.summary: Returns the platform's whole formation register, newest activity first — every org's formation, not the caller's.
get.description:
Returns the platform's whole formation register, newest activity
first — every org's formation, not the caller's. It is a Hanzo platform
operation: a caller who is not a platform reviewer gets 403.

Filter by stage and structure, page with limit and offset. An unknown stage is
refused with 400 rather than returning a silently empty page.

parameters.name: stage
parameters.description: Stage keeps only formations at that stage. Empty means any.

parameters.name: structure
parameters.description: Structure keeps only formations of that entity kind. Empty means any.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit bounds the page; 0 or less means the default of 200.

get.summary: Counts the platform's formations by stage — the register's shape in one read, so a queue that is growing is visible as a number rather than inferred by paging the list.
get.description:
Counts the platform's formations by stage — the register's
shape in one read, so a queue that is growing is visible as a number rather
than inferred by paging the list. A Hanzo platform operation: a caller who is
not a platform reviewer gets 403.

get.summary: Reports the founders whose KYC is not yet settled, oldest formation first, so the queue drains in the order founders have been waiting.
get.description:
Reports the founders whose KYC is not yet settled, oldest formation
first, so the queue drains in the order founders have been waiting. A Hanzo
platform operation: a caller who is not a platform reviewer gets 403.

It only says who is waiting; the decision itself is POST
/v1/company/kyc/decision.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit bounds how many formations are scanned; 0 or less means the default of 200.

post.summary: Skip marks the org as already incorporated and moves it onto the import path, so an existing company brings its documents and cap table in instead of forming a new entity.
post.description:
Skip marks the org as already incorporated and moves it onto the import path,
so an existing company brings its documents and cap table in instead of forming
a new entity. Available only at the structure stage.

put.summary: Records the entity kind, the state of formation and the proposed name.
put.description:
Records the entity kind, the state of formation and the proposed
name. Available only at the structure stage; an unknown structure or
jurisdiction, or an empty name, is refused with 400.

at.description: At is the unix second the filing record was written.

note.description:
Note explains a filing Hanzo did not perform itself: what remains to be done
and by whom.

provider.description:
Provider is the filing partner that performed the filing, or "manual" when no
partner is wired.

ref.description:
Ref is the partner's or the state's filing reference. Empty when nothing was
actually filed — no filing id is ever fabricated.

status.description:
Status is manual (no partner wired — a registered agent files out-of-band),
submitted (the partner accepted it, awaiting the state), filed (the state
accepted it) or rejected.

alreadyIncorporated.description:
AlreadyIncorporated declares an org that already has a legal entity, which
takes the import path (structure → import → company) instead of forming one.

capTableImported.description:
CapTableImported reports whether the existing company's cap table has been
imported onto the canonical cap table.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is the unix second the formation was opened.

documentIds.description: DocumentIDs are the data room ids of the GENERATED formation documents.

esignRef.description: EsignRef is the e-signature provider's reference for the signature request.

filing.description: Filing is the state-of-incorporation filing record, once documents exist.

founders.description: Founders is every founding stakeholder, with its equity split and KYC state.

genesis.description: Genesis is the cap-table equity genesis, once recorded.

imported.description:
Imported reports whether the existing company's corporate documents have been
ingested into the org's data room.

importedDocs.description: ImportedDocs are the data room ids of the documents ingested from Drive.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction is the state of formation: DE or WY.

name.description: Name is the company name the entity is being formed under.

org.description:
Org is the owning org — the tenant key, and the reason there is exactly one
formation per org.

paid.description: Paid reports whether the one-time formation fee has been charged.

paymentRef.description:
PaymentRef is the billing reference recorded for the charged formation fee on
the org's own ledger.

signed.description:
Signed reports whether the formation documents have come back signed — the
e-signature provider's answer, which a real provider's webhook drives.

stage.description:
Stage is the machine's current state: structure, founders, payment, documents,
esign or genesis on the formation path, import on the skip path, and company
at the terminal.

structure.description: Structure is the legal entity being formed: c-corp, llc or dao-llc.

updatedAt.description: UpdatedAt is the unix second of the most recent write to the formation.

decidedBy.description:
DecidedBy is who settled a terminal KYC status: the provider name, or a
reviewer's user id.

email.description:
Email is the founder's email, and the key a KYC decision addresses a founder
by — POST /v1/company/kyc/decision matches on it.

equityBps.description:
EquityBps is the founder's ownership in basis points, 0–10000 (1% == 100 bps,
so 10000 is the whole company). The founders' shares seed the cap-table genesis.

kycRef.description: KYCRef is the idv provider's session reference for this founder.

kycStatus.description:
KYCStatus is the founder's identity-verification state: pending, verified (a
real idv provider reported a pass), reviewer_confirmed (a privileged reviewer
confirmed out-of-band) or failed. The payment stage is unreachable until every
founder passes.

name.description: Name is the founder's full legal name, as it appears on the formation documents.

at.description: At is the unix second the genesis root was computed.

block.description:
Block is the L1 block the anchoring transaction landed in. Set only once the
receipt has been read; absent otherwise.

chainId.description: ChainID is the EVM chain the root is committed to — the Hanzo L1 by default.

note.description:
Note explains an unanchored genesis honestly — anchor wiring absent, or the
submit error — rather than reporting a commit that did not happen.

root.description:
Root is the 0x-prefixed keccak256 root of the founding allocation. It is
ALWAYS computed, whether or not the on-chain anchor is wired, because the root
is the tamper-evident witness.

status.description: Status is pending (root computed, not yet on-chain) or anchored (committed).

txHash.description: TxHash is the L1 transaction hash of the anchoring commit. Empty until anchored.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is the unix second the formation was opened.

name.description: Name is the company name the entity is being formed under.

org.description: Org is the org whose formation this row projects.

stage.description:
Stage is the formation's current state — what the platform reads to see which
formations are stalled and where.

structure.description: Structure is the legal entity being formed: c-corp, llc or dao-llc.

updatedAt.description:
UpdatedAt is the unix second of the most recent write to the formation, and
the key the register sorts on (newest activity first).

name.description: Name is the round's name on the cap table, e.g. "Seed". Required.

preMoneyValuation.description: PreMoneyValuation is the valuation the round prices off, before the new money.

pricePerShare.description: PricePerShare is the per-share price of a priced round.

roundType.description: RoundType is PRICED, SAFE or CONVERTIBLE_NOTE. Defaults to PRICED.

shareClassId.description: ShareClassID is the cap table's share class the round issues into.

targetAmount.description:
TargetAmount is the amount the round is raising, recorded verbatim on the
canonical cap table's rounds.create contract.

email.description: Email is the address the signature request is sent to.

name.description: Name is the recipient's name, as it appears on the signature request.

to.description:
To is the target stage: structure, founders, payment, documents, esign,
genesis, import or company.

alreadyIncorporated.description:
AlreadyIncorporated declares an org that already has an entity, which takes
the import path (POST /v1/company/skip) instead of the formation path.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction is the state of formation: DE or WY.

name.description: Name is the proposed company name.

structure.description: Structure is the legal entity to form: c-corp, llc or dao-llc.

email.description: Email identifies the founder on the formation.

status.description: Status is the decision: reviewer_confirmed or failed. Nothing else is accepted.

signed.description:
Signed, when present, overrides what the provider reports — the manual path
for a provider whose webhook is not wired. Omit it to take the provider's answer.

esignRef.description: EsignRef is the provider's reference for the signature request.

formation.description: Formation is the org's incorporation record with the reference recorded on it.

provider.description: Provider is the wired e-signature provider's name.

formation.description: Formation is the org's one incorporation record.

nextStages.description:
NextStages are the stages reachable from the formation's current stage,
whether or not their guards are satisfied yet.

founders.description:
Founders is every founding stakeholder. Each needs a name and an email, and
equityBps between 0 and 10000 (1% == 100 bps).

range.description: Range is an optional A1 range within the sheet; empty reads the default range.

spreadsheetId.description: SpreadsheetID is a Google Sheets id. Required.

formation.description: Formation is the org's incorporation record, now marked cap-table-imported.

rows.description: Rows is how many rows were read from the sheet, header included.

stakeholdersImported.description: StakeholdersImported is how many stakeholders the cap table accepted.

folderId.description: FolderID is a Google Drive folder id. Required.

formation.description: Formation is the org's incorporation record with the imported document ids.

ingested.description: Ingested is how many files this call put in the data room.

formation.description: Formation is the org's incorporation record with each founder's reconciled status.

provider.description: Provider is the identity-verification provider that was consulted.

email.description: Email is the founder the session belongs to.

ref.description: Ref is the provider's reference for the session.

status.description: Status is the session's status at start, which is always pending.

verifyUrl.description: VerifyURL is the hosted flow the founder visits; empty for the manual provider.

formation.description:
Formation is the org's incorporation record, with each founder's session
reference and status recorded on it.

provider.description: Provider is the wired identity-verification provider's name.

sessions.description: Sessions is one entry per founder, in the order the founders are recorded.

byStage.description: ByStage counts formations per stage, keyed by the stage name.

total.description: Total is every formation in the register.

count.description: Count is how many rows this page holds.

formations.description: Formations are the rows, newest activity first.

limit.description: Limit is the page size that was applied.

offset.description: Offset is the offset that was applied.

count.description: Count is how many founders are waiting.

queue.description: Queue is one entry per unsettled founder, oldest formation first.

roundId.description: RoundID is the cap table's id for the recorded round.

documentIds.description: DocumentIDs are data room document ids to raise a signature request over. Required.

signers.description: Signers are the recipients, each a name and an email. Required.

esignRef.description: EsignRef is the provider's reference for the signature request.

provider.description: Provider is the wired e-signature provider's name.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction is the state of formation: DE or WY.

name.description: Name is the proposed company name.

structure.description: Structure is the legal entity: c-corp, llc or dao-llc.

email.description: Email is the founder's email — the key a decision is posted against.

kycRef.description: KYCRef is the identity-verification session reference, when one was opened.

kycStatus.description: KYCStatus is the founder's unsettled status.

name.description: Name is the proposed company name.

org.description: Org is the tenant whose formation the founder belongs to.

since.description: Since is when the formation was last touched, as a unix second.
